doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

chapter: Producers, Chick's legacy and the music business
title: Working with producers like John Cale
summary: Discography talk and relations with producers, including taking over Patti Smith's mix from John Cale.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You can’t see it, but in front of my wall I printed out the Bernie Kirsh discography. And it numbers 86 — I don’t know how correct that is. And I’m wondering, on the independent things you did besides Chick, what your —
No. Starting with “Journey to Love” Stanley Clarke is the second one. It’s sort of in order.
Where did you cull these from?

I got it off the internet somewhere. I’ll send you the link and you can see what you’ve done. But I was curious about your relationships to various producers. Like going back to John Cale with Patti Smith and did you find it was different if a producer had been an engineer? Or if they had just not done that part of it?

Well the only thing is they could speak in more technical terms I guess if they had been engineers. You know, I mean John wasn’t an engineer, he was a string player. But yeah during that project I guess he had to leave the project at some point and I had to go in and take it over basically. It was just Patti and I at that point to bring it up through the mixing. So that was interesting. But he was an interesting guy, Velvet Underground and all that stuff. But technically I don’t think — that wasn’t his forte.
Did you ever have to try and tell a producer that I don’t think you want to do that?

Well it depends on what the situation is. I mean I could have a difference of opinion about something and I would approach it in a way that wouldn’t be encroaching, you know, the task is probably a greater amount of personal interaction — how shall I say — how to work with others, and how to keep things on an even keel in the control room and so forth, as much as it is a technical activity.
